schemaNotes: Brackets are [lowerBound, rate] applied to state taxable income (after std deduction and deduction-type exemptions). Rates are decimals. std.kind and exemption.kind are 'deduction' (subtract from income), 'credit' (subtract from tax) or 'none'. exemption.dependentKind is given only where the dependent item differs from exemption.kind. start is null for jurisdictions that do not tax wages. Base table = Tax Foundation 2026 table (data as of Feb 11 2026, published Feb 17 2026); entries were overridden where 2026-session laws or state revenue departments show different 2026 values (see changedFrom2025/notes). Where a state had not yet published 2026 inflation-indexed amounts, the latest published (2025) amounts are used and the state is marked verified:false.

AL.name: Alabama

std.notes: Phases down with AGI: single $3,000 at AGI <= $25,499, reduced $25 per $500 of AGI above, minimum $2,500; MFJ $8,500 at AGI <= $25,999, reduced $175 per $500, minimum $5,000.

exemption.notes: Dependent exemption $1,000 if AGI <= $50,000; $500 for $50,001-$100,000; $300 above $100,000 (TF footnote c).

AL.local: Occupational license taxes in some cities/counties, typically 0.5%-2% of wages (e.g., Birmingham 1%, Gadsden 2%); TF avg local burden 0.07% of AGI.
AL.notes: Federal income tax paid is deductible on the Alabama return. OBBBA: Alabama did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions but created its own overtime premium deduction: lesser of the overtime premium or $1,000 per taxpayer, tax years 2026-2028 (Act 2026-604).
AL.changedFrom2025: Rates unchanged. New overtime premium deduction (up to $1,000, 2026-2028).

AZ.name: Arizona

std.notes: HB 4168 (signed June 13, 2026) sets the TY2026 standard deduction at $15,750 single/MFS, $23,625 HOH, $31,500 MFJ, plus an add-on equal to charitable contributions capped at $1,000 single/$2,000 MFJ. (TF's Feb-2026 table showed $8,350/$16,700 on pre-OBBBA conformity; superseded.)

exemption.notes: No personal exemption. Dependent tax credit $125 per dependent under 17 (raised from $100 by HB 4168 for TY2026) and $25 per dependent 17+; phases out above federal AGI $200,000 single / $400,000 MFJ.

AZ.notes: Flat tax. OBBBA: HB 4168 updated IRC conformity to Jan 1, 2026 and created subtractions for federal qualified tips (IRC 224), qualified overtime (IRC 225) and the senior deduction, effective from TY2025 (decoupled from bonus depreciation).
AZ.changedFrom2025: Rate unchanged (2.5%). Standard deduction raised to $15,750/$31,500; dependent credit $100 -> $125; tips/overtime/senior subtractions added (HB 4168).

AR.name: Arkansas

std.notes: $2,470 per taxpayer (2026 DFA withholding formula).

exemption.notes: Personal tax credit $29 per taxpayer and per dependent.

AR.notes: Brackets shown are the table for net taxable income up to $94,700 (same for all filing statuses; thresholds from 2026 DFA formula). Above $94,700 a separate table applies: 2% on the first $4,700 and 3.7% on the rest, with a bracket-adjustment deduction for net income $94,701-$97,600. Top rate cut to 3.7% retroactive to Jan 1, 2026 by HB 1001/SB 1 (Acts 1-2 of the 2026 extraordinary session, signed May 2026); revised tables are inflation indexed. TF's Feb-2026 table (3.9%, $4,600/$92,300 thresholds) is superseded.
AR.changedFrom2025: Top rate 3.9% -> 3.7% (retroactive to Jan 1, 2026); thresholds indexed.

CA.name: California

std.notes: 2025 amounts (FTB); 2026 indexed amounts not yet published. TF's table showed $5,540/$11,080 (the 2024 amounts).

exemption.notes: 2025 exemption credits from Form 540 ($153 personal, $475 per dependent); 2026 indexed amounts not yet published. Credits phase out by $6 (single) / $12 (MFJ) per $2,500 of federal AGI above $252,203 / $504,411 (2025).

CA.local: No local tax on wages (San Francisco/Los Angeles levy business/payroll taxes on employers).
CA.notes: Brackets are 2025 inflation-indexed amounts (TF footnote j; 2026 indexing not published); these are also used in EDD's 2026 withholding schedules. 13.3% top rate includes the 1% Mental Health Services Tax on taxable income over $1,000,000 for all filers (hence the MFJ 12.3% step at $1,000,000). Employee SDI payroll tax (no wage cap) is separate. OBBBA: California did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions (Kiplinger).
CA.changedFrom2025: No rate change; annual inflation indexing only.

CO.name: Colorado

std.notes: Federal standard deduction (Colorado starts from federal taxable income).

CO.local: Occupational privilege taxes (flat monthly amounts) in a few cities, e.g., Denver $5.75/month employee share, Aurora $2/month.
CO.notes: Flat tax. Rate can be temporarily lowered under TABOR-surplus triggers (none reflected for 2026 in TF table). High-AGI taxpayers must add back part of federal std/itemized deductions (thresholds not verified here). OBBBA: requires add-back of the federal overtime deduction from TY2026 (HB 25-1296; a 2025 special-session bill to repeal it was postponed indefinitely); federal tips deduction flows through (Kiplinger). Initiative 195 (Nov 2026 ballot) would create a graduated tax from 2027.

CT.name: Connecticut

std.notes: No standard deduction.

exemption.notes: Personal exemption reduced $1,000 per $1,000 of CT AGI above $30,000 (single) / $48,000 (MFJ). Also a personal tax credit of 1%-75% of tax for lower AGIs.

CT.notes: Phase-out of the 2% bracket and 'tax benefit recapture' make higher-income filers pay effectively higher rates on all income.

DE.name: Delaware

exemption.notes: $110 personal credit per person.

DE.notes: Same brackets for all filing statuses.

DC.name: District of Columbia

std.notes: Tied to the federal standard deduction (TF).

DC.notes: Rates unchanged since 2022 (OTR). OBBBA: DC did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions (Kiplinger).
DC.changedFrom2025: Standard deduction follows federal inflation adjustment.

GA.name: Georgia

std.notes: Raised from $12,000/$24,000 by HB 463 for 2026 (HOH and MFS $15,000).

exemption.notes: No personal exemption; dependent deduction $5,000 for 2026 (was $4,000) per GA DOR 2026 Employer's Tax Guide and Plante Moran.

GA.notes: Flat tax. HB 463 (Act 465, signed 2026) cut the rate 5.19% -> 4.99% for tax years beginning Jan 1, 2026, with contingent 0.125-pt annual cuts toward 3.99%. TF's Feb-2026 table (5.19%, $12k/$24k, $4k) is superseded. OBBBA: partial conformity - Georgia excludes up to $1,750 of overtime pay (full-time hourly workers) and up to $1,750 of cash tips, tax years 2026-2028.
GA.changedFrom2025: Rate 5.19% -> 4.99%; std deduction $12k/$24k -> $15k/$30k; dependent $4,000 -> $5,000; new $1,750 tips and $1,750 overtime exclusions.

HI.name: Hawaii

std.notes: Act 46 (2024) schedule per Hawaii DOTAX Announcement 2024-03: $8,000 single / $12,000 HOH / $16,000 MFJ for 2026-2027 (TF's table showed the 2024-25 amounts $4,400/$8,800).

exemption.notes: $1,144 per person.

HI.notes: 2026 brackets are the same as 2025 under Act 46. Act 24 of 2026 (SB 3125) adds a 13% top rate (over $500k single / $1M MFJ) starting TY2027 - not in effect for 2026.

ID.name: Idaho

std.notes: Federal standard deduction amounts (HB 559 adopted the OBBBA standard deduction).

exemption.notes: No exemptions (Idaho has a child tax credit).

ID.notes: Flat 5.3% above a zero bracket; the $4,811/$9,622 zero-bracket amounts are TF's figures (2025 indexed; 2026 indexed amount not confirmed). Rate 5.3% confirmed by the Idaho State Tax Commission July-2026 withholding table. OBBBA: HB 559 (signed Feb 2026) conformed to the federal tips, overtime, senior and car-loan-interest deductions retroactive to Jan 1, 2025.
ID.changedFrom2025: No rate change (5.3% since 2025); OBBBA conformity incl. tips/overtime (HB 559).

IL.name: Illinois

std.notes: No standard deduction.

exemption.notes: Not allowed if AGI exceeds $250,000 (single) / $500,000 (MFJ).

IL.notes: Flat tax. OBBBA: Illinois did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions (Kiplinger).

IN.name: Indiana

std.notes: No standard deduction.

exemption.notes: $1,000 per person; qualifying dependent children get an additional $1,500 ($3,000 in the first year for some).

IN.local: County income taxes on all 92 counties: about 0.5% (Porter) to 3.0% (Randolph); Marion 2.02%, Allen 1.59%, Hamilton 1.1%, Lake 1.5% (DOR Departmental Notice #1, rates eff. Oct 1, 2026).
IN.notes: Flat tax; 2.95% for 2026 (DOR), scheduled 2.9% in 2027. OBBBA: SEA 243 (2026) excludes federal qualified tips and overtime (and car-loan interest) from state and local income tax for TY2026 only.

IA.name: Iowa

std.notes: Federal standard deduction (Iowa starts from federal taxable income).

exemption.notes: $40 personal/dependent credit.

IA.local: School district income surtaxes (a percentage of state tax set by each district) and the Appanoose County EMS surtax.
IA.notes: Flat tax since 2025. OBBBA: federal deductions incl. tips/overtime reportedly flow through via the federal-taxable-income starting point (secondary source only; not confirmed with Iowa DOR).

KS.name: Kansas
KS.notes: SB 269 revenue-trigger rate cuts were NOT triggered for 2026 (KDOR Notice 25-06).

KY.name: Kentucky

std.notes: Not doubled for joint returns; spouses filing separately on a combined return can each take $3,360 (so many couples do).

exemption.notes: No personal exemptions; low-income Family Size Tax Credit.

KY.local: City/county (and some school) occupational license taxes, commonly ~0.5%-2.5% of wages (e.g., Louisville Metro ~2.2% resident / ~1.45% nonresident; Lexington-Fayette 2.25%).
KY.notes: Flat tax; 3.5% and $3,360 confirmed by KY DOR 2026 withholding formula.

std.notes: Inflation indexed.

exemption.notes: Personal exemptions replaced by the larger standard deduction in the 2025 reform.

ME.name: Maine

std.notes: Maine Revenue Services 2026 rate schedules revised May 20, 2026 ($23,550 HOH). Phases out at higher incomes (TF 2025 thresholds: begins over $100,000 single / $200,050 MFJ). TF's table showed $8,350/$16,700; superseded.

exemption.notes: Personal exemption $5,300 per taxpayer/spouse (phases out at high income). Dependents get a refundable credit ($305 age 6+, $610 under 6 per TF, 2025 amounts), not an exemption.

ME.notes: LD 2212 (approved Apr 9, 2026) adds a 2% surcharge on Maine taxable income over $1,000,000 single / $1,500,000 MFJ, retroactive to Jan 1, 2026 (shown as the 9.15% bracket). OBBBA: Maine did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions (Kiplinger).
ME.changedFrom2025: New 2% millionaire surcharge; brackets indexed; std deduction $15,700/$31,400.

MD.name: Maryland

std.notes: Flat amount since 2025, indexed to COLA thereafter (2026 indexed figure not separately confirmed; TF shows $3,350/$6,700).

exemption.notes: Phases out between AGI $100k-$150k (single) / $150k-$200k (married).

MD.local: County/Baltimore City income tax on residents 2.25%-3.30% of MD taxable income for 2026 (e.g., Montgomery/PG/Baltimore City 3.20%, Dorchester and Kent 3.30%, Worcester 2.25%; Anne Arundel and Frederick tiered); nonresident special tax 2.25%. Max allowed rate rose to 3.3% from 2026.
MD.notes: 2% surtax on net capital gains for federal AGI over $350,000 (since 2025). Itemized deductions reduced 7.5% of FAGI over $200,000.
MD.changedFrom2025: No state rate change (6.25%/6.5% brackets added in 2025); local rate cap raised to 3.3%.

MA.name: Massachusetts

std.notes: No standard deduction.

MA.notes: 5% flat rate plus 4% surtax on income over $1,107,750 for TY2026 (mass.gov; TF showed the 2025 threshold $1,083,150). Same threshold for joint filers. Short-term capital gains 8.5%. Paid family/medical leave payroll contribution is separate.

MI.name: Michigan

std.notes: No standard deduction.

MI.local: 24 cities levy income tax, mostly 1% resident / 0.5% nonresident; Detroit 2.4% / 1.2%, Grand Rapids 1.5% / 0.75%.
MI.notes: Flat tax. OBBBA: Public Act 24 of 2025 creates state deductions for qualified overtime and qualified tips mirroring the federal deductions, tax years 2026-2028 (Treasury notice Jan 6, 2026).
MI.changedFrom2025: Exemption indexed; new tips/overtime deductions from 2026.

MN.name: Minnesota

std.notes: State-set amount (MN DOR 2026). Reduced for high AGI (TF: 3% of AGI over $244,400, 10% over $337,800, max 80% reduction).

exemption.notes: Dependent exemption only.

MN.notes: 1% surtax on net investment income over $1 million.

MO.name: Missouri

std.notes: Federal standard deduction amounts (MO 2026 withholding).

MO.local: Kansas City and St. Louis 1% earnings tax (residents and nonresidents working there).
MO.notes: Same brackets for all filers. Limited deduction for federal income tax paid (TF footnote b; percentage/caps not re-verified). Top rate 4.7% confirmed by 2026 withholding methods (trigger cut not applied).

MT.name: Montana

std.notes: Federal standard deduction (Montana starts from federal taxable income).

MT.notes: HB 337 (2025): top rate 5.65% for 2026 (5.4% in 2027); 4.7% bracket widened to $47,500 single / $71,250 HOH / $95,000 MFJ (MT DOR). Treatment of federal tips/overtime deductions not verified.

NE.name: Nebraska

std.notes: Inflation indexed.

exemption.notes: $176 personal exemption credit per person.

NE.notes: Brackets from NE DOR 2026 tax calculation schedule. Top rate scheduled 3.99% in 2027 (LB 754).
NE.changedFrom2025: Top rate 5.2% -> 4.55% (third and fourth brackets now both 4.55%).

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.notes: No tax on wages. The interest & dividends tax was repealed for tax periods beginning on/after Jan 1, 2025.

NJ.name: New Jersey

std.notes: No standard deduction.

NJ.local: No local income tax on employees (Newark levies a 1% payroll tax on employers).

std.notes: Federal standard deduction amounts.

exemption.notes: $4,000 deduction for each dependent except one (in lieu of personal exemption).

NY.name: New York

exemption.notes: Dependent exemption only.

NY.local: New York City resident tax 3.078%-3.876%; Yonkers resident surcharge 16.75% of net NYS tax and 0.5% nonresident earnings tax.
NY.notes: Tax benefit recapture applies at higher incomes (top rate applies to all income). OBBBA: FY2027 budget adopts a state exclusion of up to $25,000 of qualified tips for tax years beginning 2026; no state overtime deduction.

ND.name: North Dakota

std.notes: Federal standard deduction (ND starts from federal taxable income).

ND.notes: Bracket thresholds are 2025 indexed amounts per TF (footnote j); 2026 indexed thresholds could not be confirmed. Treatment of federal tips/overtime deductions not verified (they would flow through the federal-taxable-income start unless decoupled).

OH.name: Ohio

std.notes: No standard deduction.

OH.local: Municipal income taxes in most cities/villages, ~0.5%-3% (e.g., Columbus and Cleveland 2.5%); many school districts add 0.25%-2%.
OH.notes: IMPORTANT: statutory schedule for 2026+ is $0 tax up to $26,050, then $332 PLUS 2.75% of income over $26,050 (ORC 5747.02) - the $332 base is not captured by the bracket array. Same brackets for all filing statuses. Business income taxed separately at 3% after $250k deduction.
OH.changedFrom2025: Became flat: 2025 had 2.75% to $100k and 3.125% above (base $342); 2026 is 2.75% on all nonbusiness income over $26,050 (base $332) per HB 96.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.notes: HB 2764 (2025) consolidated brackets for 2026; further 0.25-pt cuts possible via revenue triggers.

OR.name: Oregon

std.notes: Per Oregon DOR 2026 withholding formulas.

exemption.notes: Personal exemption credit $263 per person per the 2026 DOR withholding formula (TF table showed $256, the 2025 amount). Not allowed if federal AGI exceeds $100,000 single / $200,000 MFJ.

OR.local: Portland Metro Supportive Housing Services tax 1% of taxable income over $125k single / $200k joint; Multnomah County Preschool for All 1.5% over $125k/$200k plus 1.5% more over $250k/$400k; statewide transit tax 0.1% of wages.
OR.notes: Limited subtraction for federal income tax paid (capped, phased out at higher AGI; amount not re-verified).

PA.name: Pennsylvania

std.notes: No standard deduction.

exemption.notes: No exemptions (Tax Forgiveness credit for low incomes).

PA.local: Local earned income tax (Act 32), typically ~1%-2% combined municipal + school district (higher in some cities, e.g., Pittsburgh 3%); Philadelphia wage tax 3.735% resident / 3.425% nonresident from July 1, 2026 (3.74%/3.43% before); many municipalities also levy a $52/yr Local Services Tax.
PA.notes: Flat tax on PA's own classes of income.

RI.name: Rhode Island

std.notes: Phases out between modified federal AGI $261,000 and $290,800.

RI.notes: Same brackets for all filing statuses. H.7127 (2026) millionaire surtax phases in from 2027 (top rate 6.99% 2027 rising to 8.99% 2029) - not in effect for 2026.

SC.name: South Carolina

std.notes: South Carolina Income Adjusted Deduction (SCIAD) replaces federal standard/itemized deductions: $15,000 single/MFS, $22,500 HOH, $30,000 MFJ; reduced proportionally as federal AGI rises from $40,000 to $95,000 (single), $60,000-$142,500 (HOH), $80,000-$190,000 (MFJ), fully gone above.

exemption.notes: SC dependent exemption (not repealed by Act 110; amount per TF, inflation indexed).

SC.notes: Act 110 of 2026 (H.4216), effective TY2026: 1.99% on taxable income under $30,000 and 5.21% above (SCDOR formula: 5.21% x TI - $966); brackets CPI-indexed; future revenue-triggered cuts. TF's Feb-2026 table (0%/3%/6%, $8,350/$16,700) is superseded. Starting point moved to federal AGI and federal std/itemized deductions disallowed, so federal tips/overtime deductions do not flow through.
SC.changedFrom2025: Restructured: 0%/3%/6.0% (6.2% statutory) -> 1.99%/5.21%; federal taxable income start -> federal AGI; new SCIAD deduction.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.notes: No individual income tax (Hall tax on interest/dividends fully repealed from 2021).

UT.name: Utah

std.notes: Not a deduction: nonrefundable taxpayer tax credit = 6% of the federal standard deduction ($16,100/$32,200) (or itemized deductions less state income tax) plus 6% of dependent exemptions; the whole credit is reduced by 1.3% of income over $18,213 single / $36,426 MFJ (2025 thresholds per TF; 2026 indexed values not confirmed).

exemption.notes: Dependent exemption $2,111 (per TF) is not deducted from income; it enters the taxpayer credit at 6% (~$127 per dependent) and shares the same phase-out.

UT.notes: Flat tax. SB 60 (2026) cut the rate 4.5% -> 4.45% retroactive to Jan 1, 2026 (TF's Feb-2026 table showed 4.5%).

VT.name: Vermont

std.notes: 2025 amount per TF (2026 not published); +$1,250 per federal age/blind box (2025).

exemption.notes: 2025 amount per TF.

VT.notes: Brackets/deductions are 2025 indexed amounts (TF footnotes j, n); Vermont had only published TY2025 rate schedules. Filers with federal AGI over $150,000 pay the greater of regular tax or 3% of federal AGI.
VT.changedFrom2025: Inflation indexing only (2026 figures not yet published).

VA.name: Virginia

std.notes: Virginia Tax: remains $8,750/$17,500 for TY2026; rises to $9,200/$18,400 in 2027.

VA.notes: Same brackets for all filing statuses.

WA.name: Washington
WA.notes: No tax on wages. Capital gains tax on long-term gains: 7% on gains above the annual standard deduction ($278,000 for 2025; 2026 indexed amount not confirmed), plus 2.9% (9.9% total) on gains over $1,000,000 (since 2025). SB 6346 (2026) enacts a 9.9% tax on income over $1 million (incl. wages) starting Jan 1, 2028 - under legal challenge, not in effect for 2026. WA Cares long-term-care premium 0.58% of wages and PFML premiums are payroll deductions, not income tax.

WV.name: West Virginia

std.notes: No standard deduction.

exemption.notes: $2,000 per person.

WV.local: No local income tax (some cities charge flat weekly city service/user fees).
WV.notes: SB 392 (signed Mar 31, 2026) cut all rates ~5%, retroactive to Jan 1, 2026 (WV Tax Division schedule). Same brackets for single/MFJ/HOH; MFS brackets are halved. TF's Feb-2026 table (2.22%-4.82%) is superseded.

std.notes: Sliding-scale deduction: phases out starting at $20,119 (single) / $29,039 (MFJ) income, reaching $0 at $136,453 / $159,690 (TF).
